newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of NAPM.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of NAPM.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Monday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. January personal income/consumption, February National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index and January construction spending data.
Personal income for January is forecast to show a gain of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.8 percent increase reported in December.
January personal consumption is expected to rise to 0.6 percent against December's 0.5 percent.
The NAPM for February is expected to rise to 52.9 percent from 52.0 percent. But January construction spending is expected to be unchanged from December's 0.7 percent fall.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the personal Income/consumption, NAPM index and construction spending figures for fresh clues to market direction, for more clues to market direction," a dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared their positions," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Monday/Tuesday, Tuesday/Wednesday and week-fixed were unchanged from last Friday's common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-5/16 5-3/16 and nine-months unchanged at 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
But twelve-months rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent.
